note: Ley 195 of 2020 (Gaceta Oficial Digital 29188-B, 31 December 2020), article 5, rewrote article 26 of Ley 24 of 2002 (the credit-history law): data on a consumer's credit history held by a credit information agency prescribe five years from the last payment received on the obligation, or, where nothing was paid, five years from the date the first payment fell due, and are then struck from the agency's base; the seven years of the 2002 law (as amended in 2006) no longer hold. The game reads this as five years from the late payment (keep 5), the last payment being the nearest the game holds to the law's date; a later payment that restarts the law's clock isn't modelled. Article 29-B, added by the same law, has a paid debt updated within three working days, which doesn't shorten the five years. The bureau is the Asociación Panameña de Crédito (APC), as Panamá América names it in reporting a bill to shorten the period (a secondary source for the name only). No source read states how many days after its due date a missed payment is reported, so the days are the game's reading: the bureau's next monthly update.

sources.title: Ley 195 de 2020, que modifica y adiciona artículos a la Ley 24 de 2002 (Gaceta Oficial Digital No. 29188-B, 31 de diciembre de 2020), copy on the Órgano Judicial site
sources.said: Artículo 26. Prescripción y depuración definitiva de datos. Los datos sobre el historial de crédito de consumidores o clientes incorporados en una base de datos administrada por una agencia de infonnación de datos prescribirán a los cinco años, ... contados a partir de la fecha de recepción del último pago a la correspondiente obligación, o, en caso de que no se haya efectuado ningún pago, a los cinco años, ... Transcurrido este plazo, el dato será excluido del sistema
